The PR's stated goal (make token guessing visible) needs only the method and path; the header adds nothing to it.

findings.short_summary: Export 500s on a literal JSON `null` body
findings.summary: LOW — `const { name } = body` is destructured unconditionally, so a client sending the literal JSON body `null` (valid JSON that readJson parses without error) gets a 500 instead of being treated as a missing body.
findings.failure_scenario: POST /accounts/:id/export with raw body `null` and content-type application/json: readJson() returns null (JSON.parse('null') succeeds), then `const { name } = body` throws TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'name' of 'body' as it is null, which the top-level handler turns into 500 {"error":"internal error"}. Before this diff the route never touched `body`, so it tolerated any body shape — the new destructure is the regression.

findings.short_summary: Export `name` allows path traversal out of exportDir
findings.summary: CRITICAL — the optional export `name` is checked only for type and length in src/server.js, then joined straight into a filesystem path with no sanitisation, letting any account owner write the CSV outside the configured export directory (the `path.basename` guard the old account-id path had is gone, and the response field masks where the file landed).
findings.failure_scenario: An authenticated owner of any account (role 'member' suffices) POSTs {"name": "../pwned"} to /accounts/:id/export; the server returns 200 with body {exported:0, file:'pwned.csv'} and writes pwned.csv one directory above exportDir — the directory that also holds ledger.json. Verified by direct execution against the real server using the repo's own test/helpers.js. The PR's new test at test/server.test.js:74-77 is the blind test: it exercises only a plain name and an over-length name, never one containing '/' or '..', and the pre-existing traversal test at line 86 only covers the URL's :id segment, which the route regex [^/]+ already blocks.

findings.short_summary: Caller-named exports have no containment or quota
findings.summary: CRITICAL — replacing the fixed one-file-per-account name with an arbitrary caller-chosen `name` removes the bound on how many files the endpoint can create, so a single owner can grow exports/ without limit, and the same missing containment is what lets `name` escape the directory.
findings.failure_scenario: An authenticated owner calls POST /accounts/:id/export 25 times with distinct 1-64-char names (spam-0 … spam-24); all 25 return 200 and each writes a new file, taking exports/ from 1 file to 26 for one account. There is no per-owner or per-account quota, no rate limit (MAX_BODY in src/server.js caps a single request's body size, not call frequency), and no cleanup or TTL anywhere in the repo (scripts/, .github/workflows/, README, docs/deploy.md all checked). Verified live against the running server.

findings.short_summary: Same export name across owners silently overwrites
findings.summary: HIGH — export file names form a single global namespace under exports/ with no per-owner scoping and no uniqueness check, so two unrelated owners who pick the same `name` silently clobber each other's export via a plain overwriting writeFile, with no signal to either caller.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner A POSTs {"name": "shared-report"} for their account; unrelated owner B then POSTs {"name": "shared-report"} for a different account. Both calls return 200 with no conflict indication; B's writeFile truncates and replaces exports/shared-report.csv, destroying A's exported data with no read-back endpoint to detect or recover it. Verified live with distinguishing content in each export.

findings.short_summary: Failed sign-in logs the raw Authorization header
findings.summary: HIGH — requireUser now logs ctx.req.headers.authorization verbatim on every failed authentication, printing the full bearer token for mistyped, stale or guessed-but-real credentials, which contradicts the module's own documented 'the token is never logged' guarantee.

content.text:
Run `complete`, head commit `036830a`. All five findings are this PR's own — none pre-existing. Baseline `npm run check && npm test` passed clean on the head commit, so nothing above is a pre-broken check.

**Budget** — used 18 of 20 agents (no `--agents` given, so the script took the smallest ceiling with room for every fixed angle plus two of the scout's own): 1 scout, 5 finders, 1 triage, 10 skeptics (three-lens panels on both criticals and one high, one panel shared), 1 critic. `find:tests-that-dont-test` stalled at 250s and was restarted; it completed on the retry, and the stall cost no extra agent.

**Angles** — ran security, tests-that-dont-test, data-integrity, boundary-contract, correctness; the scout sharpened the first four at the new `name` path and the new log line. It dropped three with reasons: migrations-and-rollout (no schema or persisted shape touched — `file` is a derived response value), authz-and-attribution (`requireUser` + `getOwnAccount` unchanged and still run before any effect; the traversal is a filesystem boundary, covered by security), silent-drops (`name` is never written to the store, only shaped into a path and echoed back in the same request). Nothing was cut by the ceiling, and no angle failed.

**Verification** — 10 raw findings grouped to 5 root causes; all 5 upheld, 0 refuted, 0 unverified, 0 downgraded. Three were upheld only after a skeptic **corrected** them: the two `src/export.js:18` data-integrity findings had their summaries rewritten (the containment one was originally pitched as quota-only; the skeptic established the traversal escape was the same missing guard), and the traversal finding's failure scenario was replaced with one the skeptic had actually executed. The traversal root cause was found independently by four angles; the top two findings share `src/export.js:18` because they are two consequences of one removed guard, not two code sites.

Nothing was dismissed for doubt alone, and `unverified` is empty.

**The critic found three gaps no angle covered** — these have survived no refutation, so check them by hand:

1. `test/server.test.js:64`'s title still says the export is "named for the account only", while the body it gained at lines 74-77 proves a caller can name it anything. The one artifact documenting this route's naming contract now contradicts itself.
2. The PR's second deliverable — the `src/auth.js:24-25` log line — has **no test at all**. Nothing asserts `console.warn` fires, what it logs, or that it fires only on auth failure and not on `requireRole`'s 403 path, which also runs through `requireUser`. The suite now prints three unasserted "sign-in failed" lines as a side effect.
3. README's "Known limitations" catalogue (plaintext tokens, `===`, no rate limiting) was not updated to disclose that failed attempts — including the attempted token — now flow into process logs, a destination with different retention than the ledger file it already warns about.

Result JSON written to `calibration/results/0.3.0/pr-7.json` (23.6 KB). All 18 worktrees and their branches removed; your checkout is clean at `89da56f` with only the main worktree listed. Nothing posted, per `--no-post`.
